column1: Shared memory (one memory connecting the four intelligences)
column2: 'Revenue Grid automatically and securely captures every client interaction and syncs with your CRM – turning fragmented data into a trusted source of truth for every relationship.' (https://revenuegrid.com/); 'Relationship intelligence agents provide real-time relationship context, capture insights and outcomes from previous conversations, and surface what matters most.' (https://revenuegrid.com/)
column3: 'Build agents to orchestrate actions between humans and AI.' (https://www.weflow.ai/); 'Ask anything about your calls, deals, accounts, or pipeline and get instant answers.' (https://www.weflow.ai/)
column4: Promise: 'Know every deal. Coach every rep. Forget nothing.'; one memory in three layers. Layer 1 ('What was said') is backed by Built call capture (calendar sync, transcripts, call summaries) and documents (Content Library); its email and Slack sources are In build / Planned. In build: 'Memory layers two and three: what calls meant, and what happened next'. Flagged by the Narrative: 'Connecting the dots (the pricing example)'.
column5: INTERPRETATION (analyst view, not capability claims): Overlap: both build their context on captured activity in Salesforce. Revenue Grid frames 'a trusted source of truth for every relationship' and agents that carry 'outcomes from previous conversations' into meeting prep; Weflow's Agent Builder and Ask Weflow AI work across calls, deals, accounts and pipeline. Difference: neither uses 'memory' as a headline word on the inspected pages; both centre the context on CRM records rather than on coaching or content. Opportunity (testable hypothesis): a memory that links what was said on calls to practice and approved content may be distinct from CRM-centred relationship context; test against Revenue Grid's AI Mentor memory and Knowledge Lake documentation and Weflow's Agent Builder page before claiming it. NARRATIVE V1 RECONCILIATION (Oct 20, 2026): Built today: Layer 1 call capture (calendar sync, transcripts, call summaries) and documents (Content Library). In build: memory layers two and three; email and Slack sources are In build or Planned. 'Connecting the dots (the pricing example)' is flagged by the Narrative, so the cross-layer memory story is not a public claim yet.

column1: Cross-channel intelligence (calls, CRM, emails, Slack, documents)
column2: 'Capture and sync all the client interactions that define your most valued relationships – from emails and meetings, to contacts and documents–ensuring your CRM accurately reflects the full reality of every customer relationship.' (https://revenuegrid.com/)
column3: 'Auto-capture emails, meetings, and contacts' (https://www.weflow.ai/); 'Auto-record, transcribe, and summarize meetings' (https://www.weflow.ai/); 'Record in-person conversations and use AI to auto-update Salesforce.' (https://www.weflow.ai/)
column4: Built: transcripts from Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, Fireflies, Fathom and Granola; summaries and pre-call brief delivered to Slack; documents via the Content Library. In build: reading email for deal context (Gmail, Outlook); summaries by email and Teams; meeting bot. Planned: CRM connection (Salesforce, HubSpot) and updates; reading deal conversations in Slack; deal status from email and Slack. Flagged: 'The CRM use cases'; 'Everything about email and Slack tracking'.
column5: INTERPRETATION (analyst view, not capability claims): Overlap: both capture email, meetings and contacts into Salesforce; Weflow also records, transcribes and summarises meetings and captures in-person conversations on mobile. Revenue Grid adds documents to its capture list. Difference: both are email-and-CRM-first, which is where PitchSense is weakest today. Opportunity (testable hypothesis): PitchSense should not lead on channel breadth against these two; its call-plus-document combination may matter more. NARRATIVE V1 RECONCILIATION (Oct 20, 2026): Built: transcripts from Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, Fireflies, Fathom and Granola; Slack delivery of summaries and pre-call briefs; documents via the Content Library. Email reading, Teams/email summaries and the meeting bot are In build; CRM connection and Slack deal reading are Planned. Public copy can name calls and documents only.

column2: 'Real-time visibility into pipeline health, account risk and progress, so you know what’s real and what needs action.' (https://revenuegrid.com/); 'Even committed forecasts can carry hidden risk. Instantly understand which portion of your forecast is at risk, how healthy those deals really are, and why.' (https://revenuegrid.com/product/sales-forecasting/)
column3: 'Turn customer interactions into 50+ AI insights to help your team convert and forecast deals better.' (https://www.weflow.ai/); 'Combine bottom-up, weighted, and AI forecasting' (https://www.weflow.ai/)
column4: In build: deal and account pages with connected call history; deal risks (Watch / At risk); commitments tracking. Planned: agent answers about calls, deals and accounts; CRM connection. No forecasting capability at any status. Built today: list of every call, call summaries, Home, accounts and contacts created automatically.
column5: INTERPRETATION (analyst view, not capability claims): Overlap: both sell deal and pipeline visibility with forecasting to sales leaders. Revenue Grid's Sales Forecasting page shows forecast risk and roll-ups; Weflow claims 50+ AI insights and combined bottom-up, weighted and AI forecasts. Difference: both are mature here; PitchSense has no forecasting at any status. Opportunity (testable hypothesis): PitchSense should not compete on deal visibility or forecasting against these two. NARRATIVE V1 RECONCILIATION (Oct 20, 2026): Deal and account pages, deal risks (Watch / At risk) and commitments tracking are In build; agent answers about deals and CRM connection are Planned; there is no forecasting capability at any status. Built today: the call list, call summaries, Home, and auto-created accounts and contacts. 'Know every deal' stays out of public copy.

column2: 'Use up-to-date account intelligence, meeting history and deal guidance to personalize every interaction, with easy access to engagement toolkits to help you along the way.' (https://revenuegrid.com/)
column4: Built: Content Library with AI search and sources ('One home for approved content'); practice built from your own documents. Planned: content suggested for each call and follow-up; sales content creation (one-pagers, decks, proposals in your brand guidelines). No approval-workflow or compliance-governance capability is listed at any status. Flagged: 'The security doc suggested from the Content Library'; 'Everything about creating one-pagers, decks and proposals'.
column5: INTERPRETATION (analyst view, not capability claims): Overlap: limited. Revenue Grid mentions 'engagement toolkits' alongside account intelligence and meeting history; Weflow shows no content capability on the inspected pages. Difference: neither presents a content library or content grounding on the inspected pages. Opportunity (testable hypothesis): approved content tied to calls and practice may be an open angle against both; check Revenue Grid's Help Me Write and sequence pages before treating content as absent. NARRATIVE V1 RECONCILIATION (Oct 20, 2026): Built: Content Library with AI search and sources; practice built from your own documents. Planned: content suggested per call and follow-up; sales content creation. The Narrative lists no approval or compliance workflow, and flags 'The security doc suggested from the Content Library' and 'Everything about creating one-pagers, decks and proposals'.

column3: 'Coach reps with AI feedback based on your playbook' (https://www.weflow.ai/); 'Analyzes recordings and gives feedback to help your reps run better sales meetings.' (https://www.weflow.ai/solutions/executives)
column4: Built: AI voice roleplays (11 scenario types, 3 languages, micro roleplays); tracks; skills and scoring set by Enablement; scores with evidence on every practice session; readiness per rep and scenario; coaching suggestions for managers; one-click drills with before-and-after results. In build: pre-call drill tied to a specific upcoming call. Planned: scoring real calls on your skills. Flagged: 'Checks the score on the next real call'.
column5: INTERPRETATION (analyst view, not capability claims): Overlap: Weflow coaches from real calls ('Coach reps with AI feedback based on your playbook'; an AI Coach that analyses recordings). Revenue Grid shows no coaching on the inspected pages (its Deal Guidance page, not part of this inspection, mentions AI Mentor deal coaching for managers). Difference: neither shows roleplay or practice on the inspected pages. Opportunity (testable hypothesis): practice and readiness scoring may separate PitchSense from both; test against Weflow's Conversation Intelligence coaching templates and Revenue Grid's Meetings Evaluation before claiming it. NARRATIVE V1 RECONCILIATION (Oct 20, 2026): Built: AI voice roleplays (11 scenario types, 3 languages, micro roleplays), tracks, Enablement-set skills and scoring, scores with evidence, readiness per rep and scenario, manager coaching suggestions, one-click drills. In build: the pre-call drill tied to a specific upcoming call. Planned: scoring real calls. 'Checks the score on the next real call' is flagged, so the call-tied angle is a proposal item with a date, not public copy.
